source.title: IQC Incoming Material Inspection Standard (IQC外来物料检验标准)

families.name: Packaging
families.description: Cartons, printed packs and protective packaging.

materials.name: Outer cartons
materials.summary: Paperboard, folding, dimensions and weight, shipping marks, joints, printing, damage, deformation and stains.
materials.note: The source generally specifies double-wall corrugated board unless otherwise required. Joint grading and strict dimensional boundaries need project confirmation.

rows.criterion: Paperboard quality or the number of corrugated layers does not meet the customer requirements. Unless otherwise specified, outer cartons are generally double-wall corrugated cartons.
Cracking occurs after folding back and forth 10 times.
Dimensional deviation from the shipping-mark requirements: L > 12.5 mm; H > 6.4 mm; W > 4.5 mm.
rows.note: Strict inequalities are retained. Exact boundary values and cases outside the listed bands are not assigned an acceptance decision here; confirm the project rule.

rows.criterion: The carton is too large or too small during a product trial fit, or the packed quantity does not match the reference documentation.
rows.note: The criterion calls for a trial fit; the method column itself lists only tape measure / electronic scale.

rows.criterion: The carton does not meet the engineering weight requirement of 400 g ± 10 g; for a weight greater than 400 g, follow the sample-making requirement.
rows.note: The source uses grams, not g/m². No grammage interpretation is added.

The vertical positions of the front and side shipping marks do not align.
Shipping marks on one face are not positioned symmetrically left-to-right or top-to-bottom.
The carton joint is loose or does not meet customer requirements.
rows.note: Both CR and MAJ are marked in this source row. Their priority or applicability is unresolved and must be confirmed for the project.

rows.criterion: Carton staples are arranged untidily or spaced unevenly.
The shipping-mark barcode is unclear or cannot be scanned, or there is no space for the self-adhesive barcode label.
rows.note: Scanning is specified in the criterion; the method column lists visual inspection / limit sample.

rows.criterion: Shipping-mark printing is blurred but remains readable.
rows.note: The source marks this outer-carton condition MAJ; the corresponding inner-carton condition is MIN. The difference is preserved.

rows.criterion: Shipping-mark printing is blurred and unreadable.
The shipping-mark print color is incorrect.
Damage exposes the product.
Damage does not expose the product.

Carton deformation or creasing does not affect packing, transport or appearance.
Stains affect the shipping marks, but the marks remain clearly readable.
Stains make the shipping marks unclear or unreadable.

materials.name: Color boxes
materials.summary: Paperboard and fit, text and graphics, color, printing and varnish, damage, stains, joints and barcode-label checks.
materials.note: The color-difference limit requires an agreed measurement method. The large surface-damage row has no inspection method stated.

rows.criterion: The paperboard does not meet requirements.

rows.criterion: Text or graphics are incorrect.
Text or graphics are missing from the printing.
Color does not match the sample, or the color difference from the PANTONE reference is ΔE > 0.8.
rows.note: This is the source’s stated limit. It gives no color-difference formula, instrument, illuminant, observer or measurement settings. Agree the measurement method before applying ΔE > 0.8.

rows.criterion: Printed text or graphics cannot be clearly distinguished.

rows.criterion: Obvious oil stains seriously affect appearance.

The gloss or matte level of the print varnish does not meet customer requirements.
Damage makes the product visible.

rows.criterion: Surface-layer damage is greater than 6.4 mm × 6.4 mm.
rows.note: The source leaves the item heading and the unmerged method cell blank. The damage description supplies the context. Strict inequalities are retained. Exact boundary values and cases outside the listed bands are not assigned an acceptance decision here; confirm the project rule.

rows.criterion: Stains cover graphics or text so they cannot be read.
Stains cover graphics or text, but they remain readable.
The joint is inadequately bonded and comes loose.
The serial-number label gives no result when scanned; severe trimming defects cut off text content.
rows.note: The source item is headed barcode number but its criterion says serial-number label. Scanning is in the criterion; the method column lists visual inspection / actual measurement.

Strict inequalities are retained. Exact boundary values and cases outside the listed bands are not assigned an acceptance decision here; confirm the project rule.

Strict inequalities are retained. Exact boundary values and cases outside the listed bands are not assigned an acceptance decision here; confirm the project rule.

materials.name: Polybags

rows.criterion: Material does not meet requirements.

rows.method: Visual inspection / limit sample / caliper measurement

rows.criterion: Damage area S > 6.4 mm × 6.4 mm OR length L > 25.4 mm.
rows.note: The area and length alternatives are joined by OR in the source. If their results fall into different severity bands, confirm the project decision. Strict inequalities are retained. materials.name: Blister packaging
materials.summary: Material and fit, dimensions, deformation, punctures, liquid residue, blister-to-card sealing, black specks and exposed sharp edges.

rows.note: The source states 3 pounds-force, more than 80% separation and a total over 1/2 for discontinuities. It does not define the percentage/length reference or full test procedure; confirm these before applying the rule.

materials.name: PCBA
materials.summary: Printed circuit board assemblies combine visual checks with functional/current tests and a separate solderability check.

rows.criterion: Requirement: dimensions must meet the design requirement.

Check for missing soldered components and poor solder joints; compare component arrangement with the signed sample; check cleanliness, solder residue, lifted copper, board deformation and correct switch alignment.
Check applicable functions, operating current, standby current and power-off current, where applicable, using the relevant test instruction.

rows.criterion: Requirement: complete tin wetting within 2 seconds using a 60 W soldering iron.

Requirement: book sections must be flat and orderly, without obvious splayed wrinkles, hard creases, folded corners, incomplete pages or dirt.

Requirement: page numbers and page order must be correct. Measured from the page-number center, position error must be ≤ 2.0 mm between adjacent pages and ≤ 4.0 mm throughout the book; image registration error must be ≤ 1.0 mm.
Requirement: cuts/notches in the book sections must be correctly arranged, cut through and located on the fold line.
Requirement: finished trimming skew must be ≤ 1.0 mm, with no severe blade marks, joined uncut pages or severe damage at the trimmed head.
Requirement: the finished manual must be neat, with no indentations or stains.
Requirement: appropriate adhesive viscosity; adhesive must penetrate to the innermost sheets and bond securely. Plant-based adhesives are prohibited by this source.
Requirement: no adhesive overflow; the spine must be straight, without voids, wrinkles, discoloration or damage.
Requirement: no defective, missing or double staples; binding must be flat and clean, with flat, secure staple legs and staples placed on the fold line.
Requirement: packaging must be neat, complete and undamaged, protect the product, and include the production date and an inspection pass certificate.

faqs.question: What is incoming quality control (IQC)?
faqs.answer: Incoming quality control evaluates purchased materials and components against defined requirements before their intended use in manufacturing. This page presents Xinyinhai’s internal incoming inspection standard for incoming materials, including semi-finished and finished products.

faqs.question: What sampling plan and acceptance levels does this IQC standard name?
faqs.answer: The source names MIL-STD-105E, single normal sampling inspection, General Inspection Level II, with CR 0, MAJ 0.65 and MIN 2.5. These are the source’s acceptance-level entries, not reported defect rates. This page does not calculate lot-specific sample sizes or acceptance/rejection numbers.

faqs.question: How do critical, major and minor defects differ?
faqs.answer: CR covers hazardous electrical, mechanical or appearance faults. MAJ covers functional or structural faults, or appearance problems visible at 50 cm or farther. MIN covers appearance defects visible at 25–30 cm, 45° and 5 seconds, excluding appearance-related CR defects. Inconsistent material-table marks are identified beside the relevant rows.

faqs.question: Are molding materials, color powder and wires inspection-exempt?
faqs.answer: The source is inconsistent. Its general clause temporarily exempts molding materials (胶料), color powder and “线” because the factory cannot test them, while later rows list molding-material/color-powder checks and electrical-wire checks. The exact meaning of “线” and the applicable inspection scope require confirmation; the page does not claim universal exemption or routine testing.

faqs.question: What does PCBA incoming inspection check?
faqs.answer: The PCBA section covers design dimensions, component and solder-joint appearance, cleanliness, board condition and switch alignment. It also lists relevant function and current checks, plus complete tin wetting within 2 seconds using a 60 W soldering iron. Numerical current limits must come from the applicable test instruction.

faqs.question: Can customer requirements override the general factory standard?
faqs.answer: Yes. The source says that where a customer has special requirements or requirements stricter than the factory standard, that customer’s products follow the customer requirements. The standard also references product quality standards and samples supplied by Engineering or QA.

faqs.question: Does this page provide a complete pull-test instruction for fabric?
faqs.answer: No. The source specifies warp and weft seam preparation at 10–12 stitches per inch, a 4 mm seam allowance, loading over 5 seconds and holding for 10 seconds. It does not state the target force or pass/fail force, so those must be confirmed before the test can be executed as an acceptance instruction.
